target_customer: Households in Portland, Seattle and Austin who want local farm food delivered weekly, and small farms as suppliers
problem: Small farms have poor distribution and low margins, while consumers want local food without visiting a farmers market.
business_model: Subscription and order based marketplace for local farm food; farmers deliver to micro depots and are paid for the delivery

founders.name: Julia Niiro
prior_employers: Revel Meat Co (took over the USDA inspected meat processor)
previous_startups: Wholesale company delivering meat to local restaurants
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page: digital marketing director before becoming a farmer in 2014; named a 2019 Inc. Female Founder. Education not found.

investors: Revolution Rise of the Rest Seed Fund
Revolution Rise of the Rest Seed Fund

competitors.name: Imperfect Produce
competitors.what: Venture backed weekly produce box delivery expanding to Portland
competitors.traction_then: Mobile enabled delivery boxes in Portland by mid 2019; local CSA farmers criticized its sourcing

technical_complexity.rationale: An ordering marketplace and logistics software; the hard part was the farmer delivery network, not the technology.

defensibility.rationale: Supply relationships with over 300 farms and local density helped, but each city had to be rebuilt and grocers could imitate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established box services already served Portland; no source shows a takeover or copy specifically.

market_need_then: Pandemic demand for home grocery delivery; the company reported 15x growth in 2020 (TechCrunch, November 2021).

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and community focused; tagline 'The farmers market, delivered to your door'

branding.brand_signature: The milkman model revived, with farmers making the deliveries themselves
branding.community_and_virality: Press from Bloomberg Businessweek (June 2020), GeekWire, Portland Monthly and TechCrunch; a rewards program on the site; farmer stories

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative name tied to a clear concept and several press features; confusable with a larger unrelated Australian company of the same name that collapsed in 2023.

outcome_analysis: MilkRun grew 15x in 2020 on pandemic demand, raised a 2.2 million seed in July 2020 and a 6 million Series A in November 2021, and expanded to Seattle and Austin with about 40 staff. YC now lists it as Inactive but no source gives a shutdown date or cause, so the cause is not public. Grocery and food delivery economics weakened after 2021, but no source ties that to this company.
notes: Status Inactive per YC (team size 38) but exit type is unknown because no shutdown report was found; the Australian MilkRun collapse in 2023 is a different company. Seed amount and date rest on one outlet (Built In Austin); TechCrunch gives a total of 10 million, so about 1.8 million is unaccounted for (earlier or accelerator money). CB Insights dates the Series A to May 2021, conflicting with November 2021 per TechCrunch and Business Wire. The site looked live with a 2022 footer and contained suspicious unrelated links, ignored. Competitor source for Imperfect Produce is dated mid 2019.
